detail.title: Synthesis of Predictive Processing Models in Music Experience
detail.summary: We have synthesized evidence from the Action Simulation for Auditory Prediction (ASAP) hypothesis and active interoceptive inference models to clarify how musical structure elicits emotional responses through predictive error resolution. Our findings indicate that rhythmic entrainment relies on motor simulation, while affective valence arises from the brain's attempt to resolve interoceptive prediction errors. These frameworks provide a mechanism for why music functions as a 'controlled hallucination' that engages both motor and emotional neural systems.

detail.title: Predictive Processing and Emotional Valence in Music
detail.summary: This notebook connects the ASAP hypothesis (rhythmic motor-simulation) with interoceptive inference (affective valence) to explain the dual-pathway nature of music cognition.
detail.reason: The project requirements for synthesis were met by the availability of two substantive, distinct source works. This notebook integrates these sources to move beyond the provisional research phase.
